questions.q: Of the three, women wine and songs,/ the former/ brought about his ruin.
o: Of the three, women wine and songs,
questions.s: Explanation:- Use first in place of former. Kyunki yahan teen me se sabse pehle waale ki baat karni hai isliye 'first' ka use hoga 'former' word ka use hum tab karte hain jab do me se pehle ko kehna hota hai.

questions.q:
Here, in truth, lies / the crux of the / great problem of all.

[SSC MTS Tier-01 19/05/23]
questions.s:
"great problem of all" should be corrected to "greatest problem of all."

Superlative adjectives (like "greatest") are used when comparing more than two things and indicate the highest degree.

questions.q: He has been/told many a times to/mind his manners. (SSC CHSL Tier-01 10/03/23)
questions.s: The correct idiom is "many a time" (singular) or "many times" (plural). "Many a times" is ungrammatical.

questions.q: (a) This book is /(b) undoubtedly preferable than /(c) that and its printing /(d) is also comparatively good. (e) No error
The company has recently opened (a)/ its first branch in Bangalore (b)/ and will expand its operations (c)/ to other states sooner. (d)/ No error (e)
questions.s: Use "soon" or "sooner than expected".

questions.q: He is (a) / more taller (b) / than his brother. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). 'Taller' is already comparative; 'more' is redundant. Correct form is 'taller.' Answer: (b). 'Taller' pehle se comparative hai, 'more' extra hai. Sahi form hai 'taller.' Jawab: (b).

questions.q: (a) A few word of /(b) gratitude are enough /(c) to express your /(d) feelings sincerely. /(e) No error.
The garden is (a) / very lovely (b) / in spring. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: There is no error. 'Very lovely' is correct for positive degree. Answer: (d). Sentence mein koi galti nahi, 'very lovely' positive degree ke liye sahi hai. Jawab: (d).

questions.q:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I need to (A)/ study farther (B)/ to improve (C)/ my grades. (D)
questions.s:
• Farther denotes more distant in space.

• Further means additional; more.

So, the use of 'further' will be correct to talk about additional study for the exam.

The correct sentence is - I need to study further to improve my grades.

Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.q: The Dussehra celebrations / in Mysore / this year / are grandest than / in any other part / of the state.
questions.s:
Explanation:- (c) Grandest than ki jagah par grander than those ka use hoga kyunki 'than' conjunction se pata chal raha hai ki yahan comparative degree lagani hai.

Note:- Yahan Mysore me ho rahe dussehra celebration ka comparison baaki poore state me ho rahe dussehra celebration se karna hai but yahan superlative degree ka use nahi hoga kyunki than bhi laga hai aur other bhi laga hai warna fir do part me error karna pad jaata hai aur jaisa ki aapko class me padhaya gaya hai comparative degree laga kar bhi kisi ek ka comparision ek se zyada cheezon ke sath kiya jaa sakta hai.

questions.q: The given sentence is divided into three segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error. If there is no error, select ‘No error’.
o: The committee has careful
and has decided to take action.
considered the report which you sent us
questions.s:
Correct Answer:The committee has careful

Explanation:

  • The error lies in the phrase "has careful".

  • The verb "has" should be followed by a past participle or adverb, not an adjective like "careful".

  • The correct form is: "has carefully considered", where "carefully" is an adverb modifying the verb "considered".

✅ Correct sentence:
"The committee has carefully considered the report which you sent us and has decided to take action."

Therefore, the segment with the grammatical error is: The committee has careful.

questions.q: I will give you /my notes if you promise /to return the same by Sunday.
questions.s:
Ans:- (c) replace 'the same' with 'them' 'the same' ka use adjective ke roop me kiya jaata hai par hume yahan pronoun ki zarurat hai jo 'notes' noun ko refer karega and 'to return' infinitive ka object banega.

Eg. She is the same girl that we met in the restaurant.

questions.q: Much of the art he/ discusses is funny, playing/and mischievous. (SSC MTS Tier-01 03/05/23)
questions.s: Adjectives in a series should be parallel. 'playing' should be 'playful' to match 'funny' and 'mischievous'.

questions.q: The nearest episode of the TV series airs tomorrow night.
o: of the TV series
questions.s:
The intention is to convey that the upcoming episode of the TV series will be the next one in sequence rather than the one that is physically closest, then "next" would indeed be the appropriate word choice.

The corrected sentence would be: "The next episode of the TV series airs tomorrow night."

questions.q: There are many species of parakeets in India, the (recognizable) being the Rose-ringed parakeet.
questions.s: The sentence compares one species with all others in the group, so it needs a superlative adjective.

questions.q: He is (a) / the most good (b) / player in the team. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). 'Most good' should be 'best,' the superlative form. Answer: (b). 'Most good' galat hai, sahi superlative form hai 'best.' Jawab: (b).

questions.q: (a) In his old age,/(b) a person is likely to get/(c) more weak day by day./(d) No error
This mango tree yields lot of mangoes every year.
questions.s:
(a) Explanation:-

A lot of :- quantitative adjective

A lot - adverb of degree

Lot of - wrong word

The lot of - isme 'lot' noun hai.

yhan mangoes ke liye quantitative adjective chahiye isliye ' a lot of' ka use hoga.

questions.q: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’.
o: Mine grandmother needs
No improvement required
My grandmother needs
Mine grandmother needed
questions.s:
Explanation:

  • "Mine" is an archaic or poetic form used without a noun (e.g., This book is mine). It cannot be used directly before a noun like “grandmother”.

  • The correct possessive determiner before a noun is "my" (e.g., My grandmother).

  • "Needs" is correct here (present simple) to match the subject "grandmother" (singular).

Correct sentence:My grandmother needs a helper to keep her terrace garden in order.

questions.q: Platinum is costlier than any metal found on earth.
questions.s: Explanation:- ‘Any metal’ ki jagah 'any other metal' ka use karen. kyunki jab ek noun ka comparison ek ese group se karna hota hai jiska wo khud ek part hota hai toh use exclude karna padta hai isliye yahan 'other' lagakar exclude karna padega.

questions.q: Though we both are of the same height, (a) / you are more heavier (b) / than I. (c) / No error (d)
questions.s: The error is in part (b). 'Heavier' is already comparative; 'more' is redundant. Correct form is 'heavier.' Answer: (b). 'Heavier' pehle se comparative hai, 'more' extra hai. Sahi form hai 'heavier.' Jawab: (b).

questions.q:
He dreams big than his friends.

{CHSL-24 MAY 2022 S2}
questions.s: The correct comparative form of "big" is "bigger." In this sentence, we're comparing the size of dreams between the subject and his friends, so the adjective should be in its comparative form.

questions.q: We live in a populated country of 120 million people.
questions.s:
(c) Explanation:-

populated( V2 of verb populate) meaning - kisi area me ja kar rehna

Populous (Adjective) :- area where a large number of people live.

Yhan country noun ke liye adjective ki requirement hai. Isliye populous ayega.

questions.q: None can / believe that / Ramesh is happier / than grieved to know it.
questions.s: Explanation:- Use more happy in place of happier. kyunki jab ek hi person ki do qualities ka apas me comparison hota hai, toh comparative degree 'er' wale structure se nahi 'more' wale structure se banayi jaati hi.
